title: Knowledge check: Error Handling and Reliability

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of error handling and reliability?
options: Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.

A production review covers version pinning, script integrity where applicable, useful errors, accessible behavior, tested performance, dependency updates, deployment checks, and maintainable documentation.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: A production review covers version pinning, script integrity where applicable, useful errors, accessible behavior, tested performance, dependency updates, deployment checks, and maintainable documentation.
questions.explanation: A production review covers version pinning, script integrity where applicable, useful errors, accessible behavior, tested performance, dependency updates, deployment checks, and maintainable documentation. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying defensive checks?
options: Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use defensive checks deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use defensive checks deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with error handling and reliability?
options: Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
